svg.text: claudia creates — layouts and templates: the offer on a slide (E10.4 and E10.5, reworked)
Mock round of 22 Nov 2026, for review before the architecture step and any code. Content is invented. Branch and decision ids are still to be agreed.

A layout is a named arrangement of placeholders that slides follow. Moving, resizing or deleting an object that took a placeholder changes the layout for every slide that follows it, or starts a new one.
A · Option 1: the offer appears after the change, in a quiet strip
Slide 3 overflowed in its right list, so its frame was enlarged. The strip offers the two choices; there is no “only this slide”.
Price rises passed on in Q3
You changed the frame of “Right list”.
This slide and 11 others follow “Two lists”.
More than one slide? The preview (sheet 2) opens before anything changes.
Leaving the slide without choosing could count as “Update layout”, with Undo: your call.
B · Option 2: decide the scope before editing
Like the style popover: a switch in the layout chip says where placeholder changes go.
Where a change to a placeholder goes
A new layout, made from this slide
named later, like a deviating style
The switch holds for the current popover only, as in styles.
+ no strip appearing during a drag
− a hand drag has no obvious place
to ask; the switch is easy to forget
− the default decides how often a
new layout is made by accident
C · The layout chip: choose, edit, manage
Each layout shows its name, what it is for, and how many slides follow it.
D · Format menu — a proposal; where these entries belong is a question for you
Same order as Style ▸ (Apply…, Edit…, All…). All six keys are free in claudia-menus.xlsx (version 6) and are not entered there yet.
1 · Layout ▸ and Template ▸ in Format, beside Style ▸ — or somewhere else?
2 · Save as template… writes a file: here, or under File ▸ Manage ▸ Export…?
3 · Entries are creates-only for now; computes slides (E6.31) get none.
4 · composes has named page styles (E9.14), a sibling of layouts: a
5 · The keys above are proposals; Ctrl+Alt+L / Ctrl+Alt+E were D376’s.
